# Interrupting a live log follow stops the client, not the job.
# Go contract: cli.go:292 ("interrupting does not cancel the job"), 296-301
# (follow uses the command context, not --timeout), main.go:15 (SIGINT
# cancels that context). Upstream 922a9f046c4a2714edf2b76fec3d1862dcd56ae3
# command.py:342-359 has the analogous rule for interrupted blocking
# requests: the request continues and cancellation is a separate command.
# Server, CLI and workload are all separate processes.
server start
taskfile release.json release
skygo --json run -f release.json --request-id follow
job-id JOB
await-file ready
await-state $JOB running

# Attach, wait until the client has printed live output, then interrupt it.
! skygo jobs logs $JOB --follow &
await-stdout '^first\n$'
interrupt
wait
stdout '^first\n$'
# The signal and transport cancellation paths may supply different prose.
# The stable contract is the canceled classification and unsuccessful exit.
stderr '^canceled: '
env SKYGO_EXIT_CODE
stdout '^SKYGO_EXIT_CODE=1\n$'

# The interrupt neither cancelled nor finished the job, and the workload still
# reacts to input given after the client went away.
skygo --json jobs get $JOB
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_RUNNING"'
! stdout 'cancel_requested'
mkdir release
await-file released
skygo jobs logs $JOB
stdout '^first\nsecond\n$'

# A second follower attached to the still-running job ends on its own once an
# explicit cancellation makes the job terminal.
skygo jobs logs $JOB --follow &
await-stdout '^first\nsecond\n$'
skygo --json jobs cancel $JOB --yes
stdout '"cancel_requested": *true'
wait
stdout '^first\nsecond\n$'
! stderr .
! skygo --json run -f release.json --request-id follow --wait
stdout '"id": *"'$JOB'"'
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_CANCELED"'
stdout '"reason": *"canceled by operator"'
env SKYGO_EXIT_CODE
stdout '^SKYGO_EXIT_CODE=2\n$'

server stop
! stdout .
! stderr .
